help.title: Management guide
help.lead: How to use the management screens, by profile and by screen. This guide is the software documentation: it changes with each release and cannot be edited from the management area.

first-steps.title: Getting started
first-steps.summary: Choose an edition, find your way in the side menu, find a screen, get help.
first-steps.intro: Management is organised by edition: each screen works on the chosen edition, and your rights are those of your roles in that edition.
first-steps.chooseBody: The “Edition” selector lists the editions where you hold a management role. The last one used reopens when you come back.
first-steps.railTitle: Find your way in the side menu
first-steps.railBody: Screens are grouped into categories; only the current screen's category is open. Click a heading to explore another one: the next navigation returns to the screen's category.
first-steps.searchBody: Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac) moves the cursor to the search box in the top bar. Type a screen name or a business word (“deadline”, “reviewer”), then Enter, or pick with the arrow keys.
first-steps.helpBody: The “?” button at the bottom right opens the current screen's sheet. The full guide is in the Help category of the side menu.
first-steps.activeRoleText: If you hold several roles in the edition, the “Active role” selector narrows the side menu to that role's categories. It is a display filter: your rights remain those of all your roles, checked by the server.
first-steps.versionedText: This guide documents the software: it cannot be edited from the management area and changes with each release.

security.title: Two-factor authentication and identity confirmation
security.summary: Why management asks for a code, and when it asks for your password again.
security.intro: Two-factor authentication (a six-digit code from an app such as FreeOTP or Google Authenticator) is mandatory for management roles. The server checks it on every request: without it, management is refused.
security.enableBody: My account › Security › Enable: scan the QR code, enter the code shown by the app, then keep the recovery codes somewhere safe.
security.stepUpBody: At each sign-in, enter the code from the app. A session stays valid for 12 hours at most.
security.reauthText: Some operations require an authentication less than 5 minutes old: publishing or archiving the edition, changing review confidentiality, removing a role, inviting an administrator or a conference chair. A window then asks for your password again, and the operation resumes by itself.
security.lostText: Use a recovery code. Without one, only the platform operator can reset your two-factor authentication, after checking your identity.

roles.title: Roles and rights
roles.summary: What each management role allows in an edition, and who can grant it.
roles.intro: Rights belong to an edition: a role in one edition gives nothing in another. There is no global role.
roles.admin: Edition administrator: all rights, including archiving.
roles.chair: Conference chair: settings, publication, members and invitations, audit log.
roles.scChair: Scientific committee chair: read-only settings; members and invitations of the scientific committee only.
roles.grantorsText: Administrator and conference chair: by an administrator. Scientific committee chair and organising committee members: by an administrator or the conference chair. Scientific committee members: also by that committee's chair.
roles.lastAdminText: The last active administrator of an edition cannot be removed from the management area: only the platform operator can, through a logged command.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.summary: Edition status, remaining settings, key dates, publication and archiving.
dashboard.intro: The dashboard summarises the edition: status, settings to complete before publication, key dates in the edition's time, pending invitations and the state of your two-factor authentication.
dashboard.publishBody: Possible once the list is complete: titles in French and English, conference dates, at least one active track and one active presentation type, call opening and closing dates. The server checks again and refuses otherwise, naming what is missing.
dashboard.archiveBody: Only possible after the end of the conference: the edition then becomes read-only.
dashboard.noReturnText: A published edition does not return to draft, and an archived edition cannot be reopened from the management area: only the operator can do so, with a logged reason.
dashboard.whoText: Publish: administrator or conference chair. Archive: administrator. Both require a recent identity confirmation.

settings-general.title: General information
settings-general.summary: Code, titles, theme, dates, venue and time zone of the edition.
settings-general.intro: Titles and themes are entered in French and English; English is required to publish. The time zone (IANA name, for example Africa/Abidjan) is the one in which deadlines are entered and displayed.
settings-general.timezoneText: Deadlines already entered keep their instant: their displayed local times shift. Check the calendar after any time zone change.
settings-general.readOnlyText: Only the administrator and the conference chair change the settings; other roles view them. An archived edition can no longer be changed.
settings-general.languages: Submission languages: those in which authors may write their proposal.
settings-general.frozenTitle: Code frozen after the first submission
settings-general.frozenText: As soon as a submission is sent, the edition code (prefix of the references) is frozen (RG-19). Only an administrator can change it, with a logged reason.

settings-lists.title: Tracks and presentation types
settings-lists.summary: Lists offered to authors: bilingual, ordered, can be deactivated.
settings-lists.intro: Each item has a French and an English name, a display order and an active state. Types also carry a default duration, a maximum number of words for the abstract and the expected PDF file.
settings-lists.addBody: “Add” button, then “Save”: the item takes its place according to its order.
settings-lists.editBody: Row buttons. Every change and every deletion is logged.
settings-lists.deactivateText: An item used by a submission can no longer be deleted (refusal “item in use”): deactivate it, and it disappears from the choices offered to authors.
settings-lists.publishText: At least one active track and one active presentation type are required to publish the edition.
settings-lists.filePolicy: PDF file of a type: none, optional or required, with a maximum size from 1 to 50 MB.

settings-calendar.title: Calendar
settings-calendar.summary: Key dates of the edition, entered in the edition's time.
settings-calendar.intro: Deadlines are entered in the edition's time zone; the server stores them in universal time. The screen also shows your local time when it differs.
settings-calendar.reserved: Reserved codes (call opening and closing, end of reviews, notification, camera-ready version, registration): their chronological order is checked.
settings-calendar.free: Free code: a label is then required.
settings-calendar.public: “Visible on the portal”: the date appears among the edition's public dates.
settings-calendar.orderText: A call closing date earlier than its opening, for example, is refused, with a message on the field concerned.
settings-calendar.publishText: Call opening and closing dates are required to publish the edition.

settings-confidentiality.title: Review confidentiality and settings
settings-confidentiality.summary: Double-blind review, reviewers per submission, reviewer load, divergence and final score.
settings-confidentiality.intro: In double-blind review, reviewers see neither the name, nor the address, nor the affiliation of the authors. The server removes this information, not the display.
settings-confidentiality.load: Maximum load: number of active reviews per reviewer (10 by default); beyond this, the assignment is refused.
settings-confidentiality.divergence: Divergence threshold: gap between the highest and the lowest score (out of 100) beyond which the submission is flagged in the follow-up and by e-mail to the scientific committee chair (30 by default).
settings-confidentiality.confidence: Final score: plain average of the submitted reviews, or average weighted by the confidence each reviewer declared.
settings-confidentiality.sensitiveText: The change requires a recent identity confirmation; it is logged with the before and after values.
settings-confidentiality.frozenTitle: Double-blind frozen after the first submission
settings-confidentiality.frozenText: As soon as a submission is sent, double-blind review is frozen (RG-19): authors prepared their file accordingly. Only an administrator can change it, with a logged reason.

members.title: Members
members.summary: Active and removed roles of the edition; removing a role.
members.intro: The list shows each role held in the edition. The scientific committee chair only sees that committee's members. The email address is only shown to those who manage members.
members.revokeBody: “Remove role” button, optional reason (logged), then identity confirmation. The person is notified by email.
members.historyBody: “Show removed roles” also lists removed roles, with their date.
members.addText: Members are not added directly: they are invited (Committees › Invitations).
members.refusalsText: You can only remove roles you can grant, and the edition's last administrator cannot be removed here.

invitations.title: Invitations
invitations.summary: Invite people to a role; follow up, resend or cancel.
invitations.inviteBody: Enter up to 50 addresses, the role (and the organising committee function), the email language and an optional message. Addresses already invited or already members are skipped and reported.
invitations.followBody: Filter by status: pending, accepted, declined, cancelled, expired. An invitation expires after 14 days.
invitations.resendBody: An invitation is sent three times at most. Cancelling makes the link unusable.
invitations.linkTitle: The link alone grants no role
invitations.linkText: The person must sign in, or create an account, with the invited and verified address before accepting.
invitations.sensitiveText: Inviting an administrator or a conference chair requires a recent identity confirmation.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.summary: Who did what and when, with the before and after values.
audit.intro: The log records the edition's management actions: settings, status, roles, invitations. It contains neither IP addresses nor plain email addresses.
audit.action: Filter by action: exact (edition.updated) or by prefix (role.).
audit.filters: Filters by object type and by period, dates included.
audit.actor: Actor: a user, an operations command or the system.
audit.immutableText: A log entry can be neither changed nor deleted, not even by an administrator.

portal-sections.title: Portal sections
portal-sections.summary: Create, write and reuse the portal's blocks.
portal-sections.intro: A section is a typed block, reusable on several pages. It only appears on the portal when placed on a page (Portal › Pages) and published.
portal-sections.content: Content sections (rich text, banner, image and text): you write the title, text and buttons, in French and English side by side.
portal-sections.data: Data sections (edition header, key dates, tracks, types, documents, committees): the content comes from the edition, never from a copy; you only set the title and presentation.
portal-sections.createBody: “Add a section”: choose the type and a code (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens), then complete the section.
portal-sections.editBody: The text accepts simple HTML: paragraphs, bold, italics, lists, links, subheadings. Anything else is removed when saving.
portal-sections.previewBody: “Preview” shows the text as it will be saved, after cleaning.
portal-sections.reuseText: The list of sections shows the pages each one is on: changing a section changes it everywhere.
portal-sections.deleteText: A section still placed cannot be deleted: the message names the pages; remove it from them first.

portal-pages.title: Pages and composer
portal-pages.summary: Site pages, custom pages and the order of their sections.
portal-pages.intro: The portal has two kinds of pages.
portal-pages.site: Site pages (home, call for papers, dates, tracks, committees, programme, speakers, registration): template and address set by the software; you add sections and write titles and descriptions.
portal-pages.custom: Custom pages (e.g. practical information): published under /fr/p/… and /en/p/…, made only of sections.
portal-pages.composeBody: “Compose” opens the page: choose a section and “Place at the end”.
portal-pages.orderBody: “Move up” and “Move down” buttons; “Remove” takes the section off the page without deleting it.
portal-pages.infoBody: Titles and descriptions are used for browser tabs, search engines and share previews.
portal-pages.templateText: On a site page, the template content is shown before the placed sections.
portal-pages.refusalsText: A site page cannot be deleted and keeps its address. A page in a menu cannot be deleted: remove it from the menu first. An identifier reserved for site pages is refused.

portal-menus.title: Portal menus
portal-menus.summary: Entries of the header and footer menus.
portal-menus.intro: Each entry has a label in French and English and points to a portal page or an address.
portal-menus.addBody: “Add an entry” under the chosen menu: labels, destination, optional new tab.
portal-menus.fallbackText: While a menu is empty, the portal shows its default navigation.
portal-menus.linksText: https:, mailto:, tel: or a portal address (/en/…). Others are refused. An entry to an unpublished page is not shown.

portal-publish.title: Releasing the portal
portal-publish.summary: Why a change does not appear on the portal right away.
portal-publish.intro: The portal is generated in advance (prerendered) to be fast and well indexed. A change saved in the management area only appears at the next release.
portal-publish.editBody: Write and compose in the Portal category; changes to the edition (dates, tracks, types), to the committees and each programme publication count too.
portal-publish.bannerBody: The banner of the portal screens counts unpublished changes and shows the last release.
portal-publish.deployBody: Ask the operator for a release: they regenerate the portal, then the counter goes back to zero.
portal-publish.delayText: Between saving and release, the portal shows the previous version: this is not a fault.
portal-publish.committeesText: The “Committees” page lists active members who accepted the public directory in their account; their photo only if they accepted that too. Never an email address. The others are counted (“and 2 other members”). A withdrawn consent applies at the next release.
portal-publish.whoText: Administrator, conference chair and the organising committee member in charge of communication. Other management roles can view.

portal-files.title: Documents and images
portal-files.summary: Public files of the edition, poster included.
portal-files.intro: Files added here are public by nature: once published, any portal visitor can download them.
portal-files.documents: Documents: PDF, DOCX, ODT or ZIP (LaTeX template), 10 MB at most. They appear in “Documents” sections.
portal-files.images: Images: PNG, JPEG or WebP, 5 MB at most, resized and stripped of their metadata (including GPS position). They are used by “image and text” sections and as the poster.
portal-files.uploadBody: Choose the kind, the file and its titles, then “Upload”. The file arrives unpublished.
portal-files.publishBody: “Edit”: review the titles, tick “Published”. An unpublished file is never served.
portal-files.posterBody: At the bottom of the screen: a published image becomes the image of share previews.
portal-files.refusedText: The type is checked from the content, not the name: a file whose extension does not match, an SVG, an executable or an archive too large once uncompressed is refused.
portal-files.inUseText: A file in use (section, poster) cannot be deleted: the “Used by” column says where to remove it first.

submissions.title: Submissions
submissions.summary: Filtered list, details, CSV export and extensions after the call closes.
submissions.intro: All proposals of the edition, drafts included, with their authors. The details show the metadata, the authors' addresses, the PDF versions, the declarations and the status history.
submissions.filterBody: Combine statuses, track, type and language; the search covers the reference, the title and the authors' names.
submissions.detailBody: Click the reference. Each PDF version can be downloaded; with double-blind review, the file metadata was removed on upload.
submissions.exportBody: “Export (CSV)” uses the filters shown. The file opens in a spreadsheet (separator “;”); every export is logged.
submissions.extensionBody: In the details: deadline in the edition's time and a reason, sent to the author. An extension can be revoked at any time.
submissions.draftsText: Drafts appear in the list so that an extension can be granted to an author interrupted by the closing; they have not been submitted yet.
submissions.closingText: When the call closes, submissions move to the eligibility check automatically, within the hour. A submission under extension moves when its extension ends. A submission under eligibility check can no longer receive an extension.
submissions.whoText: Viewing: administrator, chairs and organising committee. Extensions and export: administrator, conference chair and scientific committee chair.
submissions.duplicatesText: A submission is flagged when the same submitter has another one, not withdrawn, with the same title (case, accents and punctuation ignored). It is a signal, not a refusal: the author was warned before submitting.

my-reviews.title: My reviews
my-reviews.summary: Read, score, submit, discuss; decline in case of conflict.
my-reviews.intro: Each submission entrusted to you appears here once reviewing opens, with its due date. You review with the edition's grid.
my-reviews.listBody: The list shows the due date and the state of your review: to do, draft, submitted.
my-reviews.readBody: Abstract, keywords and PDF. In double-blind review, the PDF was stripped of its metadata and downloads under the reference.
my-reviews.scoreBody: Score each criterion; the indicative weighted score is shown as you type. Save the draft at any time.
my-reviews.submitBody: Required criteria, recommendation, confidence and comment to the authors are required. Each submission is a version; you can resubmit until the decision.
my-reviews.discussBody: Once your review is submitted and the discussion is open, you read the other reviews, under pseudonyms, and talk with the committee.
my-reviews.anonymityText: You never receive the authors' identity in double-blind review; the other reviewers only know your pseudonym.
my-reviews.declineText: In case of conflict of interest or unavailability, decline with a reason: the chair appoints a replacement. A submitted review can no longer be declined.
my-reviews.expertiseText: Declare your tracks of expertise in “My expertise”: they guide the assignments.
my-reviews.frozenText: Once a decision is recorded, reviews can no longer be changed; they remain readable.

review-follow-up.title: Review follow-up
review-follow-up.summary: Screening, assignments, conflicts, follow-up, discussion and decision.
review-follow-up.intro: After the call closes, submissions go through screening. The scientific committee chair assigns reviewers, opens reviewing, follows delays and divergences, then decides.
review-follow-up.assignBody: In a submission's record, choose among the available reviewers: load, expertise and conflicts are shown.
review-follow-up.screenBody: Once the required reviewers are assigned, “Admissible” opens reviewing and notifies the reviewers. “Inadmissible” rejects, with a reason sent to the author.
review-follow-up.followBody: The list flags missing reviewers and delays; the progress shows each reviewer's load and the divergences.
review-follow-up.discussBody: The discussion opens by itself when all reviews are submitted; you can open it earlier and post in it.
review-follow-up.decideBody: On a reviewed submission, record a provisional decision; it stays hidden from the authors until publication.
review-follow-up.conflictsText: A reviewer who is an author of the submission can never review it. Same institution or declared conflict: can be overridden with a reason, logged, after confirming your identity.
review-follow-up.loadText: Beyond the edition's maximum load (Settings › Confidentiality), the assignment is refused.
review-follow-up.remindersText: Reviewers are reminded automatically seven days and one day before the due date, then after it, once each.
review-follow-up.divergenceText: Beyond the edition's threshold, the submission is flagged and you receive an email; it is up to you to open the discussion or add a reviewer.

ranking.title: Ranking and decisions
ranking.summary: Simulate a threshold, decide in batch, publish, export.
ranking.intro: Reviewed submissions are ranked by final score (average of the reviews, possibly weighted by confidence), with divergence and recommendations.
ranking.simulateBody: Enter a threshold: the number of submissions kept is shown, in total, by type and by track.
ranking.batchBody: “Prepare decisions” proposes “accepted” above the threshold and “rejected” below; adjust, then save. All or nothing.
ranking.publishBody: Publication changes the statuses and notifies the authors. It asks you to confirm your identity.
ranking.exportBody: The CSV has one line per review, with the reviewer's name; each export is logged.
ranking.noReturnText: A published decision cannot be cancelled. Only a waitlisted submission can then be accepted.
ranking.authorsText: The decision, the assigned format, your message and the reviewers' comments under pseudonyms; never their names, scores or confidential comments.
ranking.waitlistText: From the submission's record, “Accept from the waiting list” notifies the authors at once.

grids.title: Evaluation grids
grids.intro: One grid per edition, and if needed one per presentation type: reviewers score each criterion on the grid's scale.
grids.createBody: The new grid uses the study's default grid; adapt it before the first review.
grids.criteriaBody: Code, French and English labels, weight and whether it is required. An optional criterion left unscored is excluded from the calculation.
grids.duplicateBody: “Duplicate” creates an editable version; reviews already made keep their version.
grids.sumText: The weights must add up to exactly 100; otherwise saving is refused.
grids.lockedText: From the first saved review, the grid can no longer be changed or deleted: duplicate it.
grids.scopeText: The latest version of the grid of the submission's type, otherwise that of the “all types” grid.

program-planner.title: Programme planner
program-planner.summary: Place confirmed papers in sessions, with the mouse or the keyboard.
program-planner.intro: The planner shows one day at a time: one column per room, sessions in time order. The “to schedule” list gathers the papers their authors have confirmed and that are not placed yet.
program-planner.poolBody: Filter the list by track or type, or search for a reference or a word of the title.
program-planner.placeBody: Drag the paper into a session, or use “Place in…” and choose the session. It is added at the end, with the duration of its paper type.
program-planner.orderBody: The arrows move a slot up or down. “Actions…” moves it to another session, changes its duration or removes it. Times are recalculated automatically, buffer included.
program-planner.conflictsBody: After each action, the server reports two sessions in the same room at the same time, a person in two places, or a session that overruns. “Show” opens the session concerned.
program-planner.keyboardText: Everything the mouse does can be done with the keyboard: “Place in…”, the arrows and “Actions…”. Each result is announced to screen readers.
program-planner.draftText: Nothing is visible to authors or the public before publication. If another member changes the programme at the same time, the screen reloads and asks you to repeat your action.
program-planner.whoText: The organising committee, the chair and the scientific committee chair consult. The administrator and the “programme” OC member edit. The chair publishes.

program-sessions.title: Sessions
program-sessions.summary: Create each day's sessions, their session roles and their free items.
program-sessions.intro: A session has a type (plenary, parallel, break…), a title, an optional room and a time. Papers are placed in it from the planner.
program-sessions.createBody: “Add a session”, then choose the type, the room and the time. Once saved, the session stays open for its roles and free items.
program-sessions.timesBody: Enter the start and end in the edition's time. The session starts during the edition's dates and lasts 24 hours at most.
program-sessions.rolesBody: Search for a person of the edition, choose their role (session chair, discussant, moderator, panellist), then add them.
program-sessions.freeBody: Invited talk, speech, award ceremony: a title, a duration and, if needed, an invited speaker.
program-sessions.timezoneText: A time that does not exist, or exists twice, in the edition's time zone (clock change) is refused: choose another time.
program-sessions.inviteText: Only people with a role in the edition are listed. First invite an outside person with the “Session chair” or “Speaker” role.
program-sessions.deleteText: Its slots and roles disappear; its papers go back to the “to schedule” list.

program-rooms.title: Rooms
program-rooms.summary: Declare the edition's rooms, their capacity and their equipment.
program-rooms.intro: Sessions take place in these rooms. The public programme shows them, with their access information.
program-rooms.equipment: Equipment: closed list (projector, microphone…) and a free note.
program-rooms.access: Accessibility: checkbox and access information, published.
program-rooms.inUseText: A room used by a session cannot be deleted: deactivate it. It disappears from the choices without changing existing sessions.

program-publication.title: Programme publication
program-publication.summary: Publish a version of the programme and follow its history.
program-publication.intro: Publication freezes the draft as a numbered version. The public programme and “My schedule” read this version, never the draft.
program-publication.checkBody: The screen shows unpublished changes, remaining conflicts and papers still to schedule.
program-publication.publishBody: The chair clicks “Publish the programme” and confirms. A new authentication may be requested.
program-publication.portalBody: The public programme is prerendered: it appears at the portal's next release. The Portal banner counts the publication among the changes to release.
program-publication.conflictsText: Publication is refused while a conflict remains (room, person, overrun), or if nothing changed since the last version.
program-publication.emailsText: Every presenter, invited speaker or session chair whose schedule is new, changed or removed receives an email, once per version.
program-publication.whoText: The chair only. Other profiles consult the status and the history.

settings-program.title: Programme settings
settings-program.summary: Buffer between slots and presenter registration.
settings-program.intro: Two edition settings frame the programme.
settings-program.buffer: Buffer: from 0 to 30 minutes between two slots of a session (RG-13).
settings-program.registration: Presenter registration (RG-11): disabled by default; when enabled, the planner flags a paper with no registered presenter, and publication is refused while any remains.
settings-program.reflowText: Changing the buffer recalculates the time of every slot. Any overrun appears in the planner.

registrations.title: Registrations
registrations.summary: Follow registrations, record a payment received, cancel.
registrations.intro: A registration is an order: category, options, promo code, price frozen when ordering. It is confirmed by a payment, a waiver or a zero total.
registrations.filterBody: By status, category, payment method or search (name, address, reference). The CSV export uses the same filters.
registrations.detailBody: The record shows the order, the proof, the documents (PDF), payments, refunds and history.
registrations.manualBody: Bank transfer or on-site payment of the full amount: the registration is confirmed and the invoice issued.
registrations.cancelBody: A reason is required. A paid registration keeps a refund due; record it once made: a credit note is issued.
registrations.statusesText: Awaiting payment, confirmed, cancelled or expired (payment deadline passed: the place and options are released).
registrations.reauthText: Manual payment, refund and export require a recent authentication.
registrations.whoText: The OC “finance” or “secretariat” members and the administrator. The Chair and other OC members consult.

payments.title: Payments
payments.intro: Every online payment attempt and every manually entered payment is listed, with its reference and the provider's.
payments.online: Online: initiated, pending, succeeded, failed or abandoned, according to the provider's notification.
payments.manual: Manual entry: bank transfer or on site, recorded from the registration record.
payments.statuses: Only a “succeeded” payment confirms a registration.
payments.webhookText: An online payment is only valid on a notification verified with the provider (RG-15); the browser's return is not enough.
payments.exportText: The CSV export is logged and requires a recent authentication.

billing-documents.title: Invoices and credit notes
billing-documents.intro: Documents are issued by the platform; their PDF is frozen.
billing-documents.invoice: Invoice: when a paid registration is confirmed.
billing-documents.creditNote: Credit note: when a refund is recorded, against the invoice.
billing-documents.proforma: Pro forma: when ordering by bank transfer, or on request; it is not an invoice.
billing-documents.numberingText: Without gaps, per series and per year: prefix, edition code, year, rank.
billing-documents.frozenText: A document is neither edited nor deleted: an error is corrected by a credit note.

finance-dashboard.title: Finance
finance-dashboard.summary: Revenue, unpaid amounts and items to handle.
finance-dashboard.collected: Collected: successful payments; net: collected minus refunded.
finance-dashboard.outstanding: Unpaid: total of the orders awaiting payment.
finance-dashboard.refundsDue: Refunds still due: due on cancellation, not yet recorded.
finance-dashboard.pendingText: Without billing details, confirmed registrations wait for their invoice. Complete the details, then “Issue pending invoices”.
finance-dashboard.orphansText: A successful payment on a cancelled or expired registration calls for a refund or an adjustment.

settings-pricing.title: Fees
settings-pricing.summary: Registration settings, categories, options, promo codes.
settings-pricing.intro: The fee depends on the category, the period (early bird, regular, on site, according to the calendar) and the zone (country of the profile).
settings-pricing.settingsBody: Currency, payment methods, local countries, payment deadlines, cancellation deadline and shares (edition time).
settings-pricing.categoriesBody: Researcher, student…; a proof may be required.
settings-pricing.feesBody: One amount per period and per zone; an empty cell is not offered.
settings-pricing.optionsBody: Local and international price, quota of places, allowed categories.
settings-pricing.promoBody: Percentage or amount, on the registration only or with options, number of uses and deadline.
settings-pricing.frozenText: An order keeps the price of the day it was placed.
settings-pricing.inUseText: A category, option or code already used cannot be deleted: deactivate it.
settings-pricing.onlineText: Offered only if a provider is configured on the server (aggregator to be chosen, Q7).

settings-billing.title: Billing details
settings-billing.summary: Issuer of the invoices and numbering.
settings-billing.intro: These details are printed on every document of the edition.
settings-billing.vat: VAT: a rate, or an exemption notice.
settings-billing.bank: Bank details: on pro forma invoices.
settings-billing.prefixes: Prefixes of invoices, credit notes and pro forma invoices, frozen from the first document of their series.
settings-billing.incompleteText: Without a company name and address, no invoice is issued (billing entity to be confirmed, Q8).
settings-billing.whoText: The OC “finance” members and the administrator, with a recent authentication.

portal.readOnly: Read-only: your roles do not allow changing the portal.
portal.codeHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (e.g. welcome).
portal.bodyHint: Simple HTML: paragraphs, bold, italics, lists, links, subheadings. Anything else is removed when saving.
portal.urlHint: https://…, mailto:…, tel:… or a portal address (/en/…).
portal.descriptionHint: Summary shown by search engines and share previews (300 characters).

typeHints.rich_text: Title, subtitle and formatted text, with one or two buttons.
typeHints.cta_banner: Call-to-action banner: title, short text and two buttons.
typeHints.image_text: An image next to a text (image: coming with public files).
typeHints.edition_hero: Title, theme, dates, venue and countdown, read from the edition.
typeHints.key_dates: The edition's public key dates, read from the calendar.
typeHints.tracks: Active tracks, read from the settings.
typeHints.submission_types: Active presentation types, read from the settings.
typeHints.committee: Members of a committee who agreed to appear on the portal.

status.howTo: The portal is generated in advance: these changes will be visible at the next release, made by the operator.
status.upToDate: The portal is up to date.
status.neverPublished: The portal has never been released yet.

sections.title: Sections
sections.lead: Reusable portal blocks: each can be placed on several pages.
sections.dataNotice: Data section: its content comes from the edition; only the title and subtitle are written here.
sections.englishFallback: An empty English column shows the French text on the English portal.
sections.previewLead: As it will be saved: tags and attributes that are not allowed are removed.

pages.title: Pages
pages.lead: Site pages and custom pages of the portal.
pages.siteLead: Template and address set by the software; you add sections to them.
pages.customLead: Free pages, published under /fr/p/… and /en/p/…, made only of sections.
pages.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: the address will be /en/p/<identifier>/.
pages.slugLocked: Fixed address for a site page.
pages.deleteMessage: “{{name}}” and its composition will be deleted. The sections remain available.

composer.title: Compose “{{name}}”
composer.siteLead: The page template is shown first, then the sections below, in this order.
composer.customLead: The page shows the sections below, in this order.

menus.title: Menus
menus.lead: Header and footer menus of the portal.
menus.empty: Empty menu: the portal shows its default navigation.

files.title: Documents and images
files.lead: Public files of the edition: templates, guides, section images, poster.
files.uploadLead: The type is checked from the file content; images are resized and stripped of their metadata. An added file is not published: publish it after review.

hints.document: PDF, DOCX, ODT or ZIP (LaTeX template), 10 MB at most.
hints.image: PNG, JPEG or WebP, 5 MB at most.

files.posterLead: Image shown in share previews (social networks, messaging apps). It must be published.
files.imageHint: Public images of the edition (Portal › Documents and images). It must be published.
files.imageUnpublished: This image is not published: it will not appear on the portal until it is (Portal › Documents and images).

submissions.title: Submissions
submissions.lead: Proposals of the edition: search, filters, details, extensions and export.

declarations.originality: Original work, not under review elsewhere

extensions.title: Extensions (RG-02)
extensions.lead: After the call closes, an extension reopens changes to this submission until its deadline. The author is informed by email.
extensions.granted: Extension granted; the author is notified by email.
extensions.revokeMessage: Changes to the submission will be refused again (planned deadline: {{date}}).

submissions.duplicatesOnly: Possible duplicates only (same author, same title)
submissions.duplicateHint: The same submitter has another submission with the same title: filter “Possible duplicates” to compare them.

reviews.title: My reviews
reviews.lead: The submissions entrusted to you. In double-blind review, the authors' identity is never sent to you.
reviews.empty: No review is assigned to you yet.

form.title: Review
form.lead: Score each criterion, then submit. The weighted score shown is indicative: the server recomputes it.
form.blind: Double-blind: the authors are not shown to you.
form.liveScoreHint: (computed as you type; the server is authoritative)
form.toAuthorsHint: Required to submit. Sent to the authors under a pseudonym, with the decision.
form.readOnly: This review can no longer be changed (assignment ended or decision made).
form.noGrid: No evaluation grid is available: notify the scientific committee chair.

submitConfirm.title: Submit the review?
submitConfirm.message: All required criteria, the recommendation, the confidence and the comment to the authors are required. You can still change it until the decision.

resubmitConfirm.title: Resubmit the review?
resubmitConfirm.message: A new version is recorded; the previous one stays in the history.

discussion.title: Discussion
discussion.summary: Final score: {{final}} / 100 · gap between reviews: {{spread}} points.
discussion.notOpen: The discussion is not open yet: it will be once all reviews are submitted, or by the chair.

decline.title: Decline the review
decline.lead: You cannot review this submission, or you have a conflict of interest? Decline it: the committee chair will appoint a replacement.
decline.conflict: I declare a conflict of interest with this submission

confirm.title: Decline the review?
confirm.message: The assignment ends; you will no longer see the submission.

expertise.title: My expertise
expertise.lead: The tracks you can review. They guide the committee chair when assigning.

followUp.title: Review follow-up
followUp.lead: From screening to decision: assigned reviewers, submitted reviews, delays and divergences.
followUp.counts: {{assigned}} reviewer(s) assigned out of {{required}} required, {{reviews}} review(s) submitted.

screening.title: Screening
screening.lead: First assign the required reviewers ({{assigned}} of {{required}}), then declare the submission admissible: reviewing opens and the reviewers are notified.
screening.reasonHint: Required to reject; sent to the author.

admit.title: Open reviewing?
admit.message: The assigned reviewers are notified by email.

reject.title: Reject the submission?
reject.message: The rejection is final; the author receives the reason by email.

candidates.title: Available reviewers
candidates.lead: Maximum load: {{max}} reviews per reviewer. Expertise matching the track is highlighted.

assign.title: Assign {{name}}
assign.dueHint: Edition time; by default, the review deadline.
assign.overrideLead: Overridable conflict of interest: give the reason for overriding it. It is logged and asks you to confirm your identity.
assign.overrideRequired: Enter the reason for overriding the conflict.

conflicts.title: Conflicts of interest
conflicts.author: author
conflicts.declared: Conflict declared; any assignment is cancelled.

decision.title: Decision
decision.provisional: provisional: hidden from the authors until publication.
decision.commentHint: Optional; sent with the decision and the reviewers' comments.

cancel.title: Cancel the provisional decision?
cancel.message: The reviews can be changed again.

promote.title: Accept the submission?
promote.message: The authors are notified at once.

ranking.title: Ranking and decisions
ranking.lead: Reviewed submissions by final score. Simulate a threshold, prepare decisions in batch, then publish the results.

simulation.title: Threshold simulation
simulation.hint: A submission is kept if its final score reaches the threshold.
simulation.result: {{accepted}} submission(s) kept out of {{total}} at the {{threshold}} threshold.

publish.title: Publish the results?
publish.message: {{count}} decision(s) become visible to the authors, who are notified by email. Publication cannot be undone.

grids.title: Evaluation grids
grids.lead: Weighted criteria of the edition, or of a presentation type. The weights add up to 100.
grids.empty: No grid: create the edition's grid.

create.title: New grid
create.lead: Created from the study's default grid (25 / 30 / 15 / 15 / 15, scores from 0 to 5), to adapt afterwards.

program.readOnly: Read only: your roles do not allow you to change the programme.
program.stale: Another member changed the programme in the meantime: it has just been reloaded. Repeat your last action if needed.

conflicts.title: Conflicts ({{count}})
conflicts.person: {{person}} is expected in two places at the same time: {{sessions}} (RG-12).

people.search: Search for a person in the edition
people.hint: At least two letters of the name.

rooms.title: Rooms
rooms.lead: Rooms of the edition: capacity, equipment, accessibility.
rooms.name: Name
rooms.accessible: Accessible to people with reduced mobility
rooms.accessNoteHint: Published in the programme and in “My schedule”.

delete.title: Delete this room?
delete.message: “{{name}}” will be deleted. A room used by a session cannot be deleted: deactivate it instead.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.lead: Sessions of each day, entered in the edition's time ({{zone}}).
sessions.instructionsHint: For speakers (“My schedule”); never in the public programme.
sessions.created: Session created: add its roles and free items.

delete.title: Delete this session?
delete.message: “{{name}}” will be deleted with its slots and roles. {{count}} paper(s) will go back to the “to schedule” list.

roles.title: Session roles
roles.inviteHint: Only people with a role in the edition are listed. For an outside person, first send a “Session chair” or “Speaker” invitation (Committees › Invitations).

planner.title: Planner
planner.lead: Place confirmed papers in sessions. Times of the edition ({{zone}}).
planner.unplaced: “{{title}}” removed from the programme: it is back in the “to schedule” list.

publication.title: Programme publication
publication.lead: Publishing freezes the programme as a numbered version: the only source of the public programme and of “My schedule”.
publication.upToDate: No changes since the last publication.
publication.effects: Placed papers become “scheduled”; every presenter, speaker or session chair whose schedule changes receives an email.
publication.chairOnly: Only the conference chair publishes the programme.
publication.portal: The public programme is prerendered: it appears on the portal at its next release.
publication.diff: Sessions: {{sessionsAdded}} added, {{sessionsChanged}} changed, {{sessionsRemoved}} removed; {{peopleNotified}} person(s) notified.

confirm.title: Publish the programme?
confirm.message: Version {{version}} will be published. Everyone whose schedule changes will receive an email. This action is logged.

registrations.title: Registrations
registrations.lead: Registrations of the edition: filter, open a record, export.

create.title: Enter a registration
create.lead: For an existing account: same rules as for the participant (quotas, promo codes, fee period; on-site fee after closing). The participant receives the order email.
create.emailHint: The account must exist and be active.
create.billingHint: Empty: name from the participant's profile.

detail.title: Registration
detail.noAction: No action available in this status.

payment.title: Offline payment
payment.lead: Bank transfer or on-site payment of the full amount (no partial payment). The registration is confirmed and the invoice issued.

waive.title: Fee waiver
waive.lead: The registration is confirmed without payment; the reason is logged.

cancel.lead: The reason is logged and sent to the participant. Refunded share: the edition's rules if left empty.
cancel.percentHint: From 0 to 100; empty: edition rule (before or after the deadline).
cancel.title: Cancel this registration?
cancel.message: Cancellation is final; the place and options are released.

refund.title: Refund
refund.lead: Refund made outside the platform (transfer, cash…). A credit note is issued against the invoice.
refund.methodHint: E.g. bank transfer, mobile money, cash.

payments.title: Payments
payments.lead: Receipts of the edition, for reconciliation.

billingDocuments.title: Invoices and credit notes
billingDocuments.lead: Documents issued (invoices, credit notes, pro forma), numbered without gaps per series.

finance.title: Finance
finance.lead: Revenue, refunds and items to handle for the edition.
finance.profileIncomplete: Billing details incomplete: no invoice is issued.
finance.orphanPayments: Successful payments on an unconfirmed registration (cancelled or expired): {{count}}
